title: Zephyr Motors pilot capture - call notes and next steps
content:
Summary:
Quick capture from 2026-03-12 call with Zephyr Motors (SaaS fleet+telematics team). They want a short pilot to validate in-vehicle diagnostics summarization + maintenance-ticket generation using private deployment (VPC) because they need data residency and offline ingest from edge gateways.

Attendees:
- Daniel Park (Zephyr) - Head of Platform
- Elena Flores (Zephyr) - Edge SW lead
- Marcus Hill (Zephyr) - Infra/Networking
- Maya Rivera (Redwood) - Solutions Eng (owner)
- Liam O'Connor (Redwood) - Infra eng (notes)
- Priya Singh (Redwood) - Security SME

Customer goals (stated):
- Proof-of-value in 6 weeks: ingest device logs -> generate short human-readable triage summaries and action items (1–3 sentences, severity tag).
- Latency target: median <= 800ms for summarization endpoint (per-vehicle single-doc, 2–6KB payload). P95 <= 2s acceptable during bursts.
- Throughput: peak 120 qps during nightly fleet-wide scans; typical steady 6–12 qps daytime.
- Data residency & isolation: must run in their AWS account within a locked VPC. No plaintext telemetry leaving their VPC.
- Compliance: SOC2 baseline acceptable; looking for KMS integration and audit logs for tokens/requests.
- Offline modes: some gateways are intermittent; they want batching/queueing and automatic replay when connectivity returns.

Notes / technical constraints:
- Edge boxes compress logs in protobuf, push to S3-like object store in the VPC. We will need an ingestion adapter (Lambda or small service) to pull, unpack, and prefix-cache frequent vehicle histories.
- Models: they are interested in smaller open models for cost predictability (mixed quantized 8-bit runs); care about hallucination on structured fields (dates, VINs).
- Hardware: They have a small fleet of on-prem GPU instances (4x A10 equivalent) in a single AZ for pilot; may be enough for initial 120 qps if batching configured; network egress to Redwood control plane must be allowed for metrics and telemetry — they are open to a private control plane peering but must sign off with security.
- Auth: SSO via Okta; API keys for service-to-service. KMS is AWS KMS; customer will provide CMK for secrets encryption.
- Observability: want per-request token cost and latency; must have request tracing to correlate with vehicle id (tokenized) and ingestion job id.

Gotchas / risks we flagged:
- VIN/PII: high risk of accidental logging of raw VINs/driver IDs. Recommend prefix/field redaction at ingestion and only surface hashed ids to model and logs. Priya flagged this as MUST for contract.
- Stateful caching: Their use-case benefits from KV cache for vehicle history but long-term growth (50k vehicles) means memory blowups if we keep unbounded cache. Need eviction policy (LRU by last-seen vehicle) and metrics to monitor hit-rate.
- Quantization/regressions: small quantized models may regress on safety/formatting of generated action items. Plan an eval suite with 200 prompt+expected-output pairs (we should propose initial seed set).
- Network topology: their infra team currently blocks outbound 443 to unknown domains; control-plane peering and allowed endpoints need ticket with NetOps; Marcus will open.

Immediate ask / success metrics for pilot:
- Working ingest -> model -> ticket-generation flow for 3 test vehicles within 2 weeks.
- End-to-end median latency <=800ms for single record path under 1 qps load.
- Demo dashboard showing per-request latency, cost, and sample outputs; 20 annotated outputs validated by Zephyr devs.

Proposed pilot architecture (sketch):
1) Ingestion: S3 (VPC) -> small puller (lambda/fargate) -> preprocessor (redact VINs, normalize telemetry)
2) Redwood Private node(s) deployed in their account (1 dedicated VPC cluster) running quantized model variant; autoscaling disabled for pilot 
3) Redis (or memcached) for short-term prefix/KV caching (hosted in same VPC)
4) Redwood control-plane peering (metrics only) or local metrics sink with push gateway if peering blocked
5) Canary routing: route traffic to local model; fallback to a hosted fallback (if allowed) for non-sensitive test datasets only

Action items (owners + due):
- Marcus (Zephyr) to open NetOps ticket for control-plane endpoints + provide VPC peering/IP allowlist by 2026-03-16.
- Maya to share pilot infra runbook + minimal infra terraform (WIP) by 2026-03-15.
- Liam to prototype preprocessor that redacts VINs and extracts 24h history samples (POC lambda) by 2026-03-19.
- Priya to draft KMS integration checklist + audit log requirements for contract language by 2026-03-18.
- Zephyr to provide 50 anonymized sample telemetry files for eval set by 2026-03-20.

Open questions we should surface in proposal:
- Will Zephyr accept hashed identifiers for request tracing instead of plaintext VINs? (security asked for confirmation).
- Are there constraints on persistent storage for KV cache (Ephemeral vs EBS)? cost sensitivity.
- What is rollback/fallback policy if local model yields format regressions — permitted to switch to hosted variant for non-PHI traffic?
- Can NetOps approve outbound to our metrics endpoint, or prefer push to customer's Prometheus?

Notes to self (short):
- Build a short eval harness: 200 prompts, split by severity, structure checks (date, VIN redaction, severity tag correct). Use it to gate quantized models.
- Keep demo outputs short and deterministic: include a fixed prompt template and post-processer to ensure formatting.
- Add a note in contract: Redwood may request ephemeral access to debug logs for 48h with customer's permission.

Meeting follow-up plan:
- Send this capture + infra runbook draft (Maya) by EOD 2026-03-13.
- Schedule architecture walkthrough with Zephyr infra + security for week of 2026-03-22.
- Setup a shared GH repo for pilot artifacts, link in ticket ZEY-123 and invite Zephyr devs.

Important links referenced during call:
- ZEY pilot ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ZEY-123
- Slack thread: #zephyr-pilot (internal)
- Example GH infra: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842

End of notes.

Unresolved / later: add concrete cost estimate for 6-week pilot (tokens + infra + engineer hours) — finance ask pending.
